note: Membership RV resort on 160 treed acres in Smoky Lake County, about 1.5 hours NE of Edmonton, with a small set of public nightly sites and cabins. Most sites are members-only or seasonal. Direct access to the Iron Horse Trail, which is used by ATVs. --Claude
summary: Operator pages + Campspot (Nov 2026): year-round, Campspot booking; base C$20 (operator page) -> C$30 (Campspot quote; W&E C$40), 30-amp + water, dump; Google 4.7/41, Campspot 5.0/3. DROP CANDIDATES: ATV trail access, membership resort with only 9 public nightly sites.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (OHV): Campspot park description: 'direct access to the Iron Horse Trail for ATV enthusiasts'. Membership FAQ: 'Are ATVs, golf carts, or off-highway vehicles allowed? Yes, but they must be used only in designated areas and routes.' Seasonal sites are sold as 'large enough to accommodate RVs up to 50 feet, including units towing off-road vehicles'. A campground adjacent to an ATV trail system is a drop candidate under the brief.

DROP CANDIDATE (membership park / long-stay tests): the home page sells a membership ('unlimited access to members-only campsites', guided sales tours with a gift, Coast to Coast campground per Campspot). The public side is 'Nightly Sites' plus cabins, 'no membership required'. Campspot offers only 9 public RV sites (24P-30P, 33P water & electric; 34P unserviced). Imagery shows roughly 75-100+ pads (a north row of ~20, a west double row of ~35+ running off the image, and a wooded eastern section), so nightly share is ~9-12%: around the 1-in-10 line, and the total was not countable. Tests 1 and 2 pass (nights on Campspot, no minimum stated); test 4 passes (FAQ: 'not permitted to use the resort or any campsite as a permanent residence').

PRICE: Campspot base C$30 unserviced / C$40 water & electric + 3% processing fee + C$3 booking fee + GST (Nov 2026). The operator page still says unserviced C$20 (undated). Under the C$69 gate either way; no gateway within 40 km (Elk Island NP 72 km).
